key_insight: Frozen weights need no capacitor or refresh; a via-programmed ROM on a generic base array cuts per-model customization to one layer.
killer_doubt: Taalas HC1 already etches Llama weights into mask ROM on TSMC N6; for capacity, 3D-NAND-based HBF is ~10x denser than 2D ROM and reprogrammable.
decisive_experiment: Cost model only, no silicon: e-beam write time for ~1e11-1e12 via shots per 300 mm wafer versus a ~$100k DUV via mask amortized over chips per model version.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 mask-ROM 'recall fabric' (AMD acquisition 2026, via search snippet); via/contact-programmed ROM; SanDisk/SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash for weights.

key_insight: Deposition-only 3D charge-shift memory with no per-bit transistor or capacitor. Writes stay in a semiconductor channel (imec: >1e10 cycles, >200 s retention). Plausibly 4-8x 1b density as a streaming tier.
killer_doubt: Charge-transfer efficiency: imec reports >98% per transfer, but 64 transfers need >=0.9999 (0.98^64 = 0.27 kept). Its 6.25 MHz clocks are ~40x below 250 MHz.
decisive_experiment: University-fab planar buried-channel (bilayer IGZO/IGO) 64-gate CCD string: measure per-transfer CTE versus fat zero at 1-100 MHz and 25-85 C. Then a 16-tier vertical coupon through an imec or NAND-pilot partner. ~$300k.
prior_art: imec 2024 'High Density 3D Buffer Memory Enabled by IGZO Channel CCD' (CTE >98%, via search snippet); 1970s Intel/Fairchild CCD main memories; Phase B N-08.

key_insight: A useful supply-chain stress test: it shows which DRAM elements (W, Hf, Zr, In, Ga) can really be substituted at trailing nodes.
killer_doubt: Without In/Ga/Zn the channel must be poly-Si. Off-current ~1e-13 A/um gives ~2 ms retention on a 1 fF node, against 64 ms or more needed.
decisive_experiment: Paper exercise first: mass per GB and available substitutes for W, Hf and Zr in a DDR5 bill of materials. Fab a ~$50k poly-Si 2T array only if a non-substitutable element appears.
prior_art: 1970s 3T silicon-gate DRAM (Intel 1103); poly-Si TFT gain cells; Mo already replacing W in 3D NAND wordlines.

key_insight: A bit-plane layout makes precision a fetch knob: score keys from the top planes, then fetch low planes only for top-k tokens, with no new silicon.
killer_doubt: Realistic KV saving is ~3-4x, not 8-12x. Every key still needs its 4 MSB planes (25-50% of K bits), and diffuse attention heads push top-k past 10%.
decisive_experiment: GPU prototype at 32-128k context: bit-plane KV layout, MSB scoring and top-k fetch. Measure bytes moved and RULER/LongBench accuracy against Quest and SparQ baselines. ~$50k compute.
prior_art: Phase B N-70 (MSB-plane sketch top-k); Quest, SparQ and Double Sparsity approximate-score KV fetch; Any-Precision LLM bit-plane weights.

key_insight: Coaxial geometry is right: C/L = 2*pi*eps/ln(r2/r1) favors a thin core, and growing electrodes rather than etching them avoids the fluorocarbon HAR etch.
killer_doubt: 2 nm ZrO2 on a 1 nm core sees 4.5 MV/cm at 0.5 V and leaks. A safe 5 nm film forces ~24 nm pitch, only ~1.5x over 864 nm2.
decisive_experiment: No devices: analytic/TCAD leakage for curved 2-5 nm ZrO2 at 1 nm radius, plus a literature yield check on single-CNT-per-site vertical growth. Kill unless both pass. ~$20k.
prior_art: Early-2000s vertical-CNT transistor and electrode research (e.g., Samsung SAIT; unverified); CNT-forest supercapacitors; Phase B N-21 grown AAO molds.

key_insight: Stranded DRAM is wafer-free capacity. Rack-scale CXL pooling plus price signals recovers part of it, which matters more at 4x prices.
killer_doubt: Microsoft Pond measured only ~7% DRAM savings from 16-socket CXL pools, not 20-30%. The added ~70-150 ns latency also limits which tenants accept pooled memory.
decisive_experiment: Replay public Azure, Alibaba and Borg traces through a pooling-plus-pricing simulator. Measure GB recovered per rack at the p99 SLO, and kill if below 15%. ~$30k.
prior_art: Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS 2023); Memtrade marketplace for harvested idle memory (SIGMETRICS 2023); CXL pooling appliances and switches (UnifabriX, XConn, Liqid).

key_insight: Retention/BER re-binning plus per-bin refresh tuning lets marginal retired dies serve as far memory. Same core mechanism as I-00224.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00224. Microsoft already runs reused DDR4 behind CXL, and re-binning likely rescues only ~5-10% more dies than pass/fail retest (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-00224: profile per-row retention of 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs at 85 C, and count dies rescued by per-bin refresh versus plain pass/fail.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU reused DDR4 via CXL (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4-capable CXL controller; ITAD resale (ITRenew/Iron Mountain).

key_insight: The fastest supply lever in the batch: an estimated ~5-7 EB/yr of DDR4 retires (~15% of 2026 bit output) and can return as CXL far memory with zero wafers.
killer_doubt: Value capture. DDR4 secondary prices rise with the 4x spike. CXL card and controller add ~$0.3-0.8/GB and 70-150 ns, and hyperscalers already reuse their own retirements.
decisive_experiment: Buy 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs, then retest and retention-profile them. Run a commercial CXL Type-3 DDR4 expander in a tier-2 cloud pilot. Report yield, landed $/GB and tiered-workload slowdown. ~$300k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 via CXL; Marvell Structera X supports DDR4 reuse; ITRenew/Iron Mountain resell decommissioned hyperscale hardware.

key_insight: The clearest economics framing of the reuse cluster: landed cost is test plus card plus controller, plausibly ~$0.5-1/GB against ~$20/GB contract DDR5.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00224. The claimed $0.05-0.15/GB leaves out the CXL card (~$0.3-0.8/GB) and the DIMM price, which tracks the shortage. Supply is capped by retirements.
decisive_experiment: Folded into the I-00224 pilot, plus Q4-2026 bid sheets from three ITAD brokers for 64 GB DDR4 RDIMMs to fix the input price.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4 reuse; ITRenew/Iron Mountain Sesame decommissioned-hyperscale resale.

key_insight: The plain form of the reuse play: keep DIMMs when servers retire and seat them in CXL expanders built on trailing-node logic.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00224 and already deployed. Latency of 150-250 ns suits only cold pages, roughly 20-40% of a typical footprint (estimate, TPP-style tiering).
decisive_experiment: Folded into the I-00224 pilot. Measure the share of pages that tolerate 200 ns under a TPP-style tiering kernel on production-like traces.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; Meta TPP tiered-memory page placement in Linux.

key_insight: Depreciated Gen-8.5 lines are real idle capital with mature IGZO know-how, and one panel has ~78x the area of a 300 mm wafer.
killer_doubt: At 2 um rules a gain cell is ~80 um2, ~90,000x a 6F2 bit. Six layers give ~15-30 GB/panel, ~$30-100/GB against a $1.48/GB DRAM cost.
decisive_experiment: Spreadsheet only: cell area at the best panel-stepper rule (~1.2-1.5 um), tiers, array efficiency and per-mask panel cost. It survives only below $5/GB, which needs imprint-scale features (Phase B N-38).
prior_art: SEL/Sharp CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; ram-venture A1-03 killed display-glass memory at 2 um; Phase B N-38 imprinted panel-level 3D oxide.

key_insight: Design for reuse is the right lever: an on-package retention and wear log makes second-life grading cheap and trustworthy.
killer_doubt: DIMMs are already socketed; the barrier is the DDR4-to-DDR5 protocol mismatch, not solder. Compression sockets add an estimated ~$1-3 per package.
decisive_experiment: Classify 500 retired DIMMs by failure cause and protocol generation. If solder or board failure is under 10% of losses, kill, and pilot the log as an SPD extension instead. ~$40k.
prior_art: CAMM2/LPCAMM2 compression-mounted modules; SPD EEPROM on every DIMM; Microsoft GreenSKU DDR4 reuse.
